sections.title: Deep learning-guided discovery reveals the diversity and mutational potential of environmental beta-lactamases
sections.abstract: The authors combine protein-language-model representations and ensemble learning to identify over 46,000 putative environmental beta-lactamases, then report resistance assays for divergent candidates and mutation effects.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim a PLM/ensemble workflow expands the candidate reservoir and identifies mutation-associated resistance changes; their abstract reports divergent candidates conferring resistance when expressed in E. coli.
sections.unique_caveat: The full text says experimental characterization covered only two class-C candidates, with resistance assessed mainly by MIC; this does not establish environmental prevalence, transmission, or human risk.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct antimicrobial-resistance relevance; the authors report expression/antibiotic testing, including MIC-based validation, rather than sequence prediction alone. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
sections.abstract: Silscore is a compact guide-sequence-only model combining global and positional duplex thermodynamics with sparse nucleotide-identity terms, evaluated on held-out and external siRNA potency datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report the highest observed Pearson correlation among evaluated comparators in three transfer evaluations, with a 26-parameter interpretable model.
sections.unique_caveat: This is retrospective dataset validation, not a prospective silencing experiment; a guide-only model omits target-site accessibility and transcript context by design.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong fit to RNA design; the paper reports evaluations on the Huesken split plus Mixset and Katoh–Suzuki external datasets and an unseen-target transfer test. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Predicting transcriptional interactions with GrnPFN
sections.abstract: GrnPFN uses a prior-data-fitted network trained on simulated gene-regulatory screens to predict non-additive transcriptional responses from single-perturbation profiles, with measured combinations added in context without retraining.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports better prediction than specified gradient-boosting and kernel-ridge baselines under low-measurement settings, including transfer to an additional perturbation screen.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that several pair folds overlap in perturbation members or compounds, some partitions reuse cells, and the additional drug–gene test covers one drug in one cell line; broader independent prospective tests are needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct relevance to gene regulation and single-cell perturbation studies; evaluated across CRISPR activation, RNA knockdown and drug-combination screens, with an additional CRISPRi–drug screen. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects
sections.abstract: MutAtlas assembles computational mutation preferences across experimentally resolved PDB structures and distills physics-based, protein-language-model, and inverse-folding signals while representing their disagreement.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim that learning relative mutation preferences while modeling disagreement improves overall performance over the tested zero-shot baselines and naive multi-source fusion methods.
sections.unique_caveat: The method is trained without experimental mutation labels and is assessed on benchmark data; model-derived mutation preferences are not biochemical measurements or clinical variant interpretations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment says accepted at ICML 2026; the authors report a ProteinGym zero-shot benchmark and release a dataset/evaluation pipeline. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: CupOFMoCA: Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly
sections.abstract: CupOFMoCA generates molecular conjugates while applying cross-component chemical constraints during generation, with computational evaluations across peptide-drug conjugate and PROTAC systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved chemically valid assembly yield versus tested post-hoc filtering and higher assembly validity on two of three PROTAC systems.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is computational generation, predicted binding/degradation scoring, and simulation; the generated molecules were not shown in the abstract to have experimentally measured degradation or therapeutic efficacy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment identifies publication in NeurIPS 2026; the abstract reports tests on three PDC systems and three PROTAC systems, including post-hoc scoring and molecular-dynamics checks. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication for Automated, Auditable Read-Level Review in Cancer Diagnostic Sequencing
sections.abstract: AVA uses auditable agent workflows to review read-level evidence for borderline low-variant-allele-frequency calls, and is evaluated on a DNA-sequencing benchmark and patient RNA-seq data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that several closed- and open-weight agents outperform the best tested VAF/depth thresholds on a subsample of borderline variants and produce reasoning traces for review.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark performance is not prospective clinical validation; the abstract does not establish impacts on diagnostic errors, turnaround time, or patient outcomes in routine laboratories.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment says accepted to the ML4H 2026 Findings Track; the abstract names the SEQC2 DNA-seq benchmark and patient RNA-seq data. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Stage-Resolved EBV-Induced B-Cell Programs Across CNS Selection and Multiple Sclerosis Compartments
sections.abstract: A cross-dataset reanalysis finds stage- and compartment-dependent EBV-associated B-cell transcriptional programs rather than a stable signature shared across blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that an early EBV-associated expression program was depleted in CSF while later latency-associated programs increased, with the directions persisting after shared genes were removed.
sections.unique_caveat: The study is a retrospective reanalysis with small evaluable samples for key contrasts; the factor did not predict MS activity (AUC 0.487), and the results do not establish causation or a validated biomarker.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines human and humanized-mouse datasets with multiple control analyses; the abstract reports nine evaluable human CSF participants and five EBV-exposed mice for key contrasts. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
sections.abstract: The authors test whether protein language models preserve contact predictions after a global amino-acid relabeling that leaves alignment-level statistics unchanged, reporting marked degradation across models and scales.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim the perturbation exposes reliance on canonical residue identities (“alphabet anchoring”) rather than only invariant coevolutionary statistics.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational invariance stress test; it demonstrates sensitivity of model outputs to token relabeling, not a direct experimental failure of protein structure prediction in biological settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted to the ICBINB failure-modes workshop at NeurIPS 2026 per the arXiv comment; tests cover ESM-2, MSA Transformer, and AMPLIFY from 8M to 3B parameters. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
sections.abstract: An energy-pixels model estimates how large a focused second-generation DNA-encoded library may need to be to sample local chemical neighborhoods and provide enough tight binders for affinity-model training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim their estimates translate the number of tight binders needed by a model into a library-size requirement without structural information or a control library as large as the experiment.
sections.unique_caveat: The approach rests on an additive “pixel” model and affinity distributions from a naive library; predicted library requirements and yields need experimental validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It directly addresses data design for protein-binding models and appears in both machine-learning and biomolecular categories; its abstract gives an explicit route to compare active-learning yield with a random-library baseline. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
sections.abstract: This review proposes a framework for describing where biological foundation models and agentic workflows are reliable, organized around data, architecture, training, evaluation, and post-analysis.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose standardized descriptions of model limits so researchers and model-using agents can state the conditions under which outputs may be trusted.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a review and framework proposal, not a new controlled comparison or a validated operational standard.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment says it is to be published in Annual Review of Biomedical Data Science; its subject is broad evaluation reliability across sequence, protein, and single-cell models. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: A Feasibility Study of Whole-Cerebrum Task-Based fMRI at 0.55 T: Motor and Visual Tasks Using Single-Shot EPI
sections.abstract: A six-participant feasibility study reports detectable motor and visual task fMRI at 0.55 T and improved signal statistics when two five-minute runs are combined.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report task activations at 0.55 T and suggest longer acquisition can compensate for lower intrinsic BOLD sensitivity in their tested setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The sample is small and healthy; the 3 T reference is described as representative rather than a matched cohort. The result does not establish clinical utility or broad reproducibility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is the latest medical-physics batch’s directly biomedical imaging feasibility paper; the abstract reports six healthy participants, both tasks, and a comparison to a representative 3 T dataset. Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Computational biology models are being tested against molecular constraints and biological datasets, but the papers predict different targets and do not jointly establish a general AI-biology capability. Silscore and GrnPFN address distinct RNA problems: potency prediction and non-additive perturbation responses. The beta-lactamase study, AVA, and the EBV reanalysis show different evidence levels—limited functional assay, sequencing-benchmark comparison, and retrospective human/mouse reanalysis. A single 0.55 T fMRI feasibility paper does not signal a broader field shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Follow-up work should test predicted beta-lactamase function across a blinded panel spanning enzyme classes, with expression controls, MIC and direct hydrolysis assays, then evaluate evolutionary accessibility under defined exposures. Silscore and GrnPFN need frozen-model prospective tests that hold out targets, cell lines, perturbation pairs, and laboratories; include target accessibility for siRNA and independent screens for perturbation prediction. MutAtlas should be assessed against new deep-mutational-scanning experiments across protein families absent from its benchmark. AVA needs blinded multi-laboratory evaluation with expert adjudication and prespecified false-positive, false-negative, auditability, and turnaround metrics. The low-field fMRI result needs a larger same-subject 0.55 T/3 T cohort with test–retest analysis. These are proposals prompted by reported limitations, not clinical advice.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This batch is strongest in computational methods for molecular and perturbation biology, with several papers making their evidence boundary visible. The clearest experimental result is limited enzyme testing; the RNA, protein-variant, diagnostic, and conjugate-design claims remain dataset- or model-based. Treat the ranking as a relevance-led reading list, not a popularity chart or clinical evidence assessment.
